question.problem:
Find the first two non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x-8{x}^{2}).$

$\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x-8{x}^{2})=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,\frac{56{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯$
question.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x-8{x}^{2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((1+2x)(1-4x)) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

For the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we recall the standard result

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & =x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To obtain the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x),$ we replace $x$ with $2x$ in the standard expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x) & =(2x)-\frac{1}{2}(2x)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(2x)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(2x)^{4}+⋯ \\  & =2x-\frac{1}{2}(4{x}^{2})+\frac{1}{3}(8{x}^{3})-\frac{1}{4}(16{x}^{4})+⋯ \\  & =2x-2{x}^{2}+\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}-4{x}^{4}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x),$ we replace $x$ with $-4x$ in the standard expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) & =(-4x)-\frac{1}{2}(-4x)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(-4x)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(-4x)^{4}+⋯ \\  & =-4x-\frac{1}{2}(16{x}^{2})+\frac{1}{3}(-64{x}^{3})-\frac{1}{4}(256{x}^{4})+⋯ \\  & =-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-64{x}^{4}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the two series to give the desired result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-2x-8{x}^{2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-4x) \\  & =(2x-2{x}^{2}+\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯)+(-4x-8{x}^{2}-\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯) \\  & =(2-4)x+(-2-8){x}^{2}+(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{64}{3}){x}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =-2x-10{x}^{2}-\frac{56{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
